_doc: Food Inflammation Index (FII) parameter table — the single source of which signals enter the per-food inflammatory-potential score, each one's direction and weight. Every parameter is scored on an ENERGY basis, per 100 kcal (the per-100 g value × 100 / max(kcal per 100 g, `minKcalPer100g`)), the energy-density adjustment of the energy-adjusted dietary inflammatory index (Hébert 2019) and of the NRF9.3 balance score: a food's water content then neither concentrates (dry pasta) nor dilutes (cooked pasta, fresh ginger) its profile. `minKcalPer100g` is the energy floor for that conversion, so a near-zero-energy food (water, salt, black coffee, tea) standardises against 20 kcal/100 g instead of dividing by ~0 — its z-scores then stop at the ±clampZ caps, and salt still reads pro through its sodium; the same floor (as kcal per gram) weights a food in the recipe aggregate (src/core/inflammation.ts), so the energy-weighted mean of per-food tags approximates the dish's own per-kcal profile. Adapted from the Food Inflammation Index idea (Wang 2024) to the composition columns this archive holds; directions are taken from open biomarker literature, NOT the licensed DII per-parameter effect scores. `dir` is +1 pro-inflammatory / -1 anti-inflammatory; `weight` scales a parameter's contribution. Read by src/core/fii.ts and scripts/build-inflammation-reference.mjs. Two parameters are DERIVED, not read straight off the vector: `fatQuality_g` = (monoFat+polyFat) − (satFat+transFat) so fat is scored once by quality instead of letting a food's saturated and unsaturated fractions cancel under independent z-scores; `freeSugar_g` = max(0, sugar − 2·fibre) estimates the free-sugar fraction from the 1:2 fibre:free-sugar dual carbohydrate-quality ratio, so a whole food's intrinsic, matrix-bound sugar is not penalised the way a refined sugar is.

parameters.cite: fat quality (MUFA+PUFA − SFA−trans), derived from the fat fractions: Wang 2024 FII

polyphenols (key anti driver): Cassidy 2015; Dryer-Beers 2024; Wang 2024 FII. One-sided: referent centre pinned at 0 (no measurable polyphenols = baseline, so a low-polyphenol food never reads pro) and scale = the median content of the foods that carry a Phenol-Explorer value (the typical polyphenol-bearing food ≈ 1 unit anti); fixed 100 mg per 100 kcal scale only while coverage is <50 foods (Pérez-Jiménez 2010)

free-sugar estimate = max(0, sugar − 2·fibre), the 1:2 fibre:free-sugar dual carbohydrate-quality ratio (Liu 2020; Drewnowski 2022); intrinsic matrix-bound sugar is not penalised (Della Corte 2025; Reyneke 2025)
